title: Batista2022: Motor-imagery EEG during NeuRow VR/haptics BCI training
description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy volunteers performing cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery of a bimanual rowing task during brain-computer interface training. The study compared Graz and NeuRow virtual-reality conditions with optional haptic and head-mounted-display feedback. Peripheral signals (ECG, respiration, PPG, accelerometry) were also recorded. This BIDS version was re-released via MOABB from the original Zenodo deposit.
methods_description: 32-channel EEG was recorded at 500 Hz with a Brain Products LiveAmp 32 and actiCAP active Ag/AgCl electrodes (10-20 montage), plus ECG, respiration and auxiliary channels. Each participant completed one session of up to five imagery runs (MI, MIMO, MIMOHP, MIMOVR, MIMOVRHP) with 5 s cue-based left/right-hand motor imagery trials and online feedback.
